leftEvidence.title: A man wrestles with Jacob, who speaks of seeing God

points.label: Figure named
points.left: Genesis calls the opponent a man within the encounter.
points.right: Hosea calls the figure an angel while recalling struggle, weeping, and Bethel.

points.label: Human response
points.left: Jacob asks for blessing, receives a new name, and names the place Peniel.
points.right: Hosea turns the memory toward returning, kindness, justice, and waiting for God.

payload.posture: Hold both Scripture sources together while preserving their participants, setting, sequence, genre, and inference boundaries.

rightEvidence.title: Hosea says Jacob struggled with the angel

payload.tension: The later prophetic witness identifies the opponent with angel-language not used for him in Genesis 32.
payload.title: Jacob’s opponent named differently in later memory
